newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends higher, Brent hits resistance.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends higher, Brent hits resistance.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed higher on Thursday while Brent maintained its gains in a market sustained by a fresh lead from the U.S. gasoline market.
September gas oil finished up $3.75 at $173.75, a dollar below the day's high but still $2 up on its opening level.
The contract held steady versus Brent ending at a $4.09 crack spread premium for September contacts.
September Brent, expiring at the close of business on Thursday, by 1645 GMT stood 17 cents up at $19.16 a barrel, the middle of the day's range.
Dealers said Brent had found resistance at the high of $19.29 a barrel.
"The market is still trending higher but it found some resistance and there hasn't been much follow through from crude on NYMEX this afternoon," said a broker.
Dealers said tight U.S. gasoline markets, helped by an outage at Exxon's Baytown, Texas refinery, were firing the rest of the oil complex.
Weekly oil inventory data released on Tuesday by the American Petroleum Institute for the week ended August 8 showed U.S. gasoline stocks near historical lows for the time of year.
Traders said buoyant U.S. gasoline prices were tempting cargoes transatlantic from the tight European market.
Brent also found support earlier on Thursday from news of a lower programme of loadings scheduled for the North Sea system in September.
Equity holders said they had been notified of a 35.5-cargo programme, down three standard cargoes from August.
Cash Brent spreads moved higher as a result.
